open_points.subject: change_staff_status
open_points.text: change_staff_status: [BEHAVIOR] MUST allow only the transitions the staff status transition table lists: active to suspended or disabled, pending_verification to active, suspended to active or disabled, and none from disabled; and MUST apply the revocation cascade; suspension or disabling revokes sessions/challenges and commits the status change plus one catalog audit atomically.
open_points.other_text: Suspension and disabling MUST additionally revoke every session of that account that is neither revoked nor expired at the same captured timestamp, because suspending or disabling an account ends its sessions and outstanding challenges; the outstanding challenges that entry also names have no persistence while that slice is deferred, so this function revokes none of them by declaration rather than by omission.
open_points.question: Must suspension or disabling revoke outstanding challenges, or must this function revoke none of them because they have no persistence?

open_points.subject: resolve_staff_session
open_points.text: resolve_staff_session: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST open its transaction with an explicit assignment, never as a context manager, and read only through tx.staff_access(): first the persisted session addressed by the identifier parsed out of the token, then the staff account that session names.
open_points.other_text: It MUST roll back exactly once immediately after the second of those two reads and mark the local open flag closed before it evaluates either result, so that a decidable rejection is never answered as a storage failure.
open_points.question: May the persisted session result be evaluated to obtain its staff_id before the account read, and what should happen when no session exists, or must neither result be evaluated until both reads have completed?
